data.reason: Modem lost ISP sync at 02:01:44 (T3 timeout), re-registered and has been OPERATIONAL since ~02:28-02:29 per modem-events/modem-metrics. The WAN watchdog is in observe mode so it only logged "would_reload" at 02:30 and 02:40 and never renewed the WAN. gw.lan still holds the old lease (fixed-address 198.51.100.27) and cannot reach the ISP gateway 198.51.100.1 (100% ping loss). Reconfiguring the WAN / renewing the DHCP lease now that the modem is operational should restore internet.

data.component: WAN interface / DHCP lease on gw.lan (vtnet0) after a cable-modem re-registration
data.cause: The cable modem lost ISP sync around 02:01 (T3 timeout), dropped and re-registered as a new session (~02:28), but the firewall's WAN interface kept its stale pre-outage DHCP lease; since the WAN watchdog runs in observe mode it only logged "would_reload" (02:30, 02:40) and never renewed the lease, so traffic to the ISP gateway black-holes even though the modem is now OPERATIONAL.
evidence: /var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-events.jsonl shows 'No Ranging Response received - T3 time-out' at 02:01:44, a TFTP config-file failure at 02:14, and 'Cable Modem Reboot ... registration complete' at 02:28:21 — the modem cycled and re-registered during the outage
/var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-metrics.jsonl: cm_status NOT_SYNCHRONIZED at 02:06, then OPERATIONAL at 02:29 and 02:40 with healthy SNR (min_snr 37.6–37.9) — the modem itself recovered before I looked

/var/db/wan-watchdog/events.jsonl: decision 'none / modem_not_operational' at 02:06, 'none / modem_settling' at 02:29, then only 'would_reload' entries at 02:30 and 02:40 with mode=observe — no reload was ever applied
/var/db/wan-watchdog/state.json: last_action 'reload', reloads_in_outage 2, modem_uptime 2280s — consistent with a modem that rebooted ~02:02 and a watchdog that never acted

ifconfig vtnet0 shows inet still 198.51.100.27 (link up), and /var/db/dhclient.leases.vtnet0 holds the old pre-outage lease (dhcp-server-identifier 203.0.113.67, renew not due until 2026/3/5) — stale WAN configuration
ping -c 3 to the ISP gateway 198.51.100.1: 100% packet loss, while arp -a still has an entry for it — stale L2/session state, path broken through the re-registered cable plant
data.recommendation: Renew the WAN DHCP lease on gw.lan (wan_reload) now that the modem is OPERATIONAL again — this was already requested and its preconditions were met. A modem power-cycle is not needed since it re-registered on its own at 02:28; the only missing step is re-acquiring the WAN address through the new modem session. Longer term, consider letting the watchdog enforce its reload decision instead of observe-only mode, so post-recovery outages self-heal.
